analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 5, 2026)
key_insights: JPM reads the post-midterm 'Blue Tsunami' as a flatter geopolitical risk curve on Iran, constraints on data centers and greater fiscal discipline. All three are seen as positive for rates, since less AI-related and UST issuance should lower long-end term premia.
Global oil balance is back in surplus at +1.4 mbd in October versus about +1.3 mbd on average last year. Lower Brent and gas risk premia should ease pressure on central banks.
The broadening trade (SXXP, SPW and SPX ex AI) is favored: earnings and fundamentals are solid, sentiment is low, election uncertainty has cleared and post-election seasonality is favorable.

The author's view is that buyside capex expectations for Tech and AI have clearly peaked. Headwinds named are funding pressure, questions over AI ARR trends and concerns over moratoria, local opposition and a possibly more restrictive regulatory environment.

JPM's Gokul argues AI infra can bounce: fundamentals are solid (unit economics, scaling laws, token growth), valuations already imply imminent EPS cuts, and classic cycle-peak signals such as inventory builds or shorter lead times are absent.
The author does not expect a return to the 1H backdrop, and expects dispersion to remain a feature.
Themes that could lead: broadening, SX7E (banks), Solar & Renewables, ACA Subsidy Exposed stocks and Cloud (existing capacity becomes more valuable), versus Federal Government Contractors.
India is a candidate at the country level given earnings, oil, its anti-AI characteristics and valuations. FII flows have been significant in recent days.

FX is called probably the best and most convex hedge if the AI unwind accelerates, because years of international inflows into USD corporate assets are poorly hedged while FX implied vol is low. Gold may be worth revisiting.

BoE is expected to hike 25bps today in a 7-2 vote. Allan expects the BoE to raise its 2026 growth forecast from 1.1% to 1.4%, driven by Q3 strength (expected annualized GDP growth of 0.3%, with 3% now looking more likely).

Asian Tech stocks are back to July 2026 levels, the fourth 20%+ correction in this rally since 2022. The team stays optimistic on unit economics, AI scaling laws and token demand, valuations that already signal EPS cuts, and the absence of cycle-peak signals.
Euro area headline inflation rose 0.2pt to 4.0% y/y, in line with JPM and consensus. Energy inflation rose 1.8pt to 20.8% y/y, food inflation rose 0.2pt to 1.6%, and core was broadly stable.
UK business equipment spending is up 14% from its 2024 low. JPM's AI-focused output indicator suggests a 0.2-0.3pt boost to UK GDP growth over the past year, not yet large historically.

Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on global equities, preferring long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus Europe. The US is described as overheating, Europe as recovering from stagflation.
Broadening can return more clearly in the US than the EU. EU earnings are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but stability in EGB spreads is needed for conviction in the EU.

Longs: Tech and supercycle themes (inference, semi cap, less-levered hyperscalers, AI-vulnerables including application software), EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners, EU pharma, UKX, selective consumer.
Shorts: AI-vulnerable ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, Autos, Chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, MedTech and MDAX.
Prime Time monthly wrap: October was a very poor month for hedge funds, traced mainly to AI/Tech, even though broad US and European indices were flat to up.
Global HF net returns were down about 4% on a rolling 20d basis as of last Friday, with MTD at -2.6% through Oct 29. The global long-short spread was -2.2% MTD (Asia -1.5%, N. Am. -1.9%, EMEA -2.4%).

Prior -3z events in the 20d L-S spread saw positive forward 20d spreads in 6 of 7 cases (avg +1%). De-grossing has been prevalent, especially in Multi-Strats, and Momentum exposure is at over 12-month lows.

US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to the 33rd percentile as of Oct 29. Retail sentiment is at the 6th percentile, ETF flows are positive (+1z) and CTA US equity positioning is at the 44th percentile.
The Split Congress Pair (JPMSC26P) rallied to 2-year highs. US Banks have a strong November seasonal record, Financials ETFs had the strongest inflows last week, and HFs remain net long Banks.

Social media sentiment and the TMT-Defensives spread are both at the 6th percentile, similar to prior episodes (late Mar '26, Mar/Apr '25, early Aug/Sep '24, late Apr '24, end Dec '22) when Tech-led weakness was followed by Tech-led rebounds.

HFs flipped to buying Biotech and Med Tech, with Health Care flows the strongest of any sector last month. HFs kept selling Utilities despite a rally, leaving them with the lowest net positioning of any major industry.
EU positioning hit the 5th percentile then rebounded to the 14th. China/HK positioning is the most bearish of any major region at the 5th percentile.
